name: excise
description: Penobscot Bay Brewing Co. (fictional) beer excise filings: the excise rate schedule, taxable removals from bond, the period operations reports (production rollforward) and the excise returns. Synthetic demo data; all money in integer cents and all volume in integer barrels. No wholesale-customer data is exposed; the controls reconcile volumes and money by period only.
domain: beer excise tax: rate schedule, taxable removals, operations reports and excise returns
notes: All money is INTEGER CENTS; all volume is INTEGER BARRELS (a US beer barrel is 31 gallons, the federal excise unit).

The excise rate is DATA, not code: tax_rates carries rate_cents_per_barrel with an effective_date. A control reads the row whose effective_date is the latest on or before the period it reconciles, so a rate change is a new row, not a new signed ruleset.
A period is the YYYY-MM filing period. Taxable liability for a period is SUM(removals.barrels) for that period times the applicable per-barrel rate.

The operations report rollforward must tie: opening_barrels + produced_barrels - removed_barrels - loss_barrels = closing_barrels. Its removed_barrels must also equal the tax return's barrels_reported for the same period.

due_date is the 15th of the month after the period (27 CFR 25.297 for beer). A return whose filed_date is after its due_date is a late filing; a period with activity and no return is a missing filing.
loss_barrels is destruction, spillage and shrinkage. Loss as a fraction of produced_barrels, in integer basis points, above tolerance is a diversion signal.

The customer_accounts table (wholesale-account names, addresses and license numbers; patient-registry IDs in a cannabis build) is intentionally omitted: this engine never reads customer data. The filings identify product by class and period only.
